title: Devcontainer: coding-agent toolchain, hooks and git wrapper
summary: Rebuilds the devcontainer image around a pinned, checksum-verified toolchain (moon, gh, actionlint, uv, Node 22, pnpm, Bun, the four coding agents, dsh) and wires every coding agent's own hook system to `osf hook` through root-owned, read-only config. The git wrapper stops relying on a system-wide core.hooksPath and instead forces /opt/factory/githooks on the command line for repositories under the workspace mount, and a set of build-time tests now prove the wrapper, the hooks and each agent binary work for the non-root `dev` user.

nodes.label: Developer
nodes.summary: The human running a coding agent inside the container. Unchanged by this diff, but the reason every hook and wrapper exists.

nodes.label: devcontainer.json
nodes.subtitle: workspaceMount → /workspace
nodes.summary: Now pins workspaceMount and workspaceFolder to /workspace, the same path the Dockerfile's WORKSPACE_ROOT build arg and OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT env var name, and extends postCreateCommand to check moon, node and pnpm.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.subtitle: +409 lines
nodes.summary: The bulk of the change: pinned, SHA-256-verified installs of moon, gh, actionlint, uv, Node 22, pnpm via corepack, Bun, the four coding agents and dsh; root-owned read-only hook config for each agent; a read-only cargo toolchain; and build-time test scripts.

nodes.label: Pinned toolchain
nodes.subtitle: moon, gh, actionlint, uv, node, pnpm, bun
nodes.summary: Every binary is downloaded from its own release tarball and checked against a published SHA-256 before install, so a rebuild in a month installs the same tool a reviewer just tested against.

nodes.label: SkillSpector / SkillEvaluator
nodes.subtitle: uv tool install at pinned commits
nodes.summary: Installed from NVIDIA git history at pinned commits for `osf lint skill`. UV_TOOL_DIR and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR are moved under /opt/factory so the dev user can read and execute them.

nodes.label: osf binary
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/osf
nodes.summary: Built from the workspace and installed root-owned, mode 0555. It is the single command every hook and git hook calls.

nodes.label: git wrapper
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/git
nodes.summary: Refuses --no-verify and -n on commit and --no-verify on push, then forces core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on the command line for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT. The system-wide core.hooksPath is gone, so a scratch repo under /tmp is no longer affected.

nodes.label: Root-owned git hooks
nodes.subtitle: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push
nodes.summary: Each hook file only calls osf. They are now reached through the wrapper's forced hooks path rather than a system git config.

nodes.label: agents.json
nodes.subtitle: the one list of agents
nodes.summary: Declares the default builder (dsh), each agent's binary, roles, hook events, hook method and hook path, plus a `gap` field where an agent's own hook system cannot express one of osf hook's two events. Tests read this file instead of naming an agent in code.

nodes.label: Claude Code
nodes.subtitle: claude
nodes.summary: Wired through /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json, a system-level settings file confirmed from the installed binary's own strings. Supports both stop and prompt.

nodes.label: Codex
nodes.subtitle: codex
nodes.summary: Wired through /etc/codex/config.toml plus a managed hooks directory forced by requirements.toml. Codex's HookEventName enum has no turn-end event, so only user_prompt_submit is wired.

nodes.label: opencode
nodes.subtitle: opencode
nodes.summary: Wired through /etc/opencode/opencode.json, which names the plugin built from integrations/opencode and copied to /opt/factory/opencode-plugin. Stop only.

nodes.label: omp
nodes.subtitle: omp (runs on Bun)
nodes.summary: omp has no system-level hooks location, so its stop hook is a root-owned, read-only directory under the dev user's own home at ~/.omp/agent/hooks/osf-stop, with the rest of ~/.omp left dev-writable.

nodes.label: dsh
nodes.subtitle: default builder
nodes.summary: Installed from its own lockfile at /opt/dsh. Its "factory" profile registers the writing-check plugin for stop and the Claude-format hooks bridge for prompt. The profile directory is root-owned and read-only; only cordis.yml stays dev-owned because dsh rewrites it on every start.

nodes.label: .claude/hooks.json
nodes.subtitle: prompt bridge target
nodes.summary: The dsh prompt bridge reads its configPath relative to the launch directory, never the profile directory, so its target cannot be a root-owned home-relative file. It points at this repo-tracked file instead, which dev can edit — the one gap in the otherwise root-owned hook wiring.

nodes.label: osf hook
nodes.subtitle: prompt | stop
nodes.summary: The single command every agent hook invokes. It supports exactly two events, prompt and stop; there is no pre-tool-use event, so none is wired.

nodes.label: /workspace
nodes.subtitle: bind mount of the repo
nodes.summary: The one folder the git wrapper treats as the workspace. devcontainer.json binds the repo here and OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT carries the same value into the wrapper, so the two files never name it separately.

nodes.label: dev user
nodes.subtitle: non-root, no sudo
nodes.summary: Runs every agent and every git command. Gets its own writable CARGO_HOME while the rustc/cargo toolchain stays root-owned, and owns ~/.omp and ~/.dsh except for the carved-out hook directories.

nodes.label: Build-time tests
nodes.subtitle: 5 scripts run during docker build
nodes.summary: git-wrapper.sh, dsh-starts.sh, coding-agent-tools.sh, builder-tools.sh and agent-hooks.sh run inside the build so a broken wrapper, a missing binary or an unwired hook fails the build instead of shipping quietly.

nodes.label: devcontainer-image workflow
nodes.subtitle: .github/workflows
nodes.summary: Builds the devcontainer image in CI, so the same pinned toolchain and the same build-time tests run on every change to .devcontainer.

nodes.label: docs/development.md
nodes.subtitle: +174 lines
nodes.summary: Documents what each git hook checks, how to run it by hand, what the git wrapper cannot do, and how to pick a builder agent via OSF_DEFAULT_BUILDER.

edges.label: workspaceMount
edges.summary: devcontainer.json now names /workspace explicitly as both the mount target and the workspace folder.
Each tool is fetched from its own release tarball and verified against a published SHA-256 before install.
uv installs both NVIDIA tools from pinned git commits, with UV_TOOL_DIR and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR moved out from under root's home.
The Dockerfile installs exactly the agents agents.json lists, each pinned to one exact npm version.
osf is still built from the workspace outside /workspace and installed root-owned, mode 0555.
The wrapper is still installed root-owned and read-only, but the system-wide core.hooksPath line it used to rely on is gone.
The three hook files are still copied to /opt/factory/githooks root-owned and mode 0555.
Five test scripts run during the build, each as the dev user where the test needs to prove dev can run the tool.
managed-settings.json is copied to /etc/claude-code and made root-owned, mode 0444.
config.toml, requirements.toml and the managed hook file are copied to /etc/codex and made root-owned, mode 0444.
The built plugin is copied to /opt/factory/opencode-plugin and opencode.json to /etc/opencode, both root-owned and read-only.
The stop hook is copied into ~/.omp/agent/hooks/osf-stop, then chowned back to root and made read-only while the rest of ~/.omp stays dev-owned.
The factory profile's package.json, cordis.patch.yml and the built plugin are copied in, then the whole profile directory is chowned to root and made read-only except cordis.yml.

edges.label: prompt bridge configPath
edges.summary: The prompt bridge resolves its configPath relative to the launch directory, so it points at the repo-tracked .claude/hooks.json rather than a root-owned file.

edges.label: stop, prompt
edges.summary: Claude Code's managed settings invoke `osf hook` for both events osf hook supports.

edges.label: prompt only
edges.summary: Codex has no turn-end event, so only user_prompt_submit reaches osf hook.

edges.label: stop
edges.summary: The opencode plugin named in /etc/opencode/opencode.json calls osf hook on stop.

edges.label: stop
edges.summary: The root-owned global extension under ~/.omp/agent/hooks/osf-stop calls osf hook on stop.

edges.label: stop, prompt
edges.summary: The factory profile's own plugin handles stop and the Claude-format bridge handles prompt, both reaching osf hook.

edges.label: OSF_DEFAULT_BUILDER=dsh
edges.summary: No script in the image chooses a builder by name; every one reads OSF_DEFAULT_BUILDER, which agents.json's default_builder mirrors.

edges.label: git commit / git push
edges.summary: Every git call under /workspace goes through the wrapper, which is first on PATH via /opt/factory/bin.

edges.label: core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
edges.summary: The wrapper now passes the hooks path on the command line for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, replacing the system-wide core.hooksPath that used to apply to every repository including a test's own scratch repo under /tmp.

edges.label: OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT
edges.summary: The wrapper reads OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT to decide whether a repository sits under the workspace mount, so a repo elsewhere is left alone.
Each hook file is a one-line call to osf; the checks themselves live in the binary.
git-wrapper.sh proves the refusals and the forced hooks path at build time.
agent-hooks.sh reads agents.json rather than naming an agent in its own code, and checks each hook file is root-owned and read-only.
dsh-starts.sh proves dsh boots on both profiles with no credentials, stopping at the missing credential and nothing else.
The new workflow builds the image, so the pinned toolchain and the build-time tests run on every change to .devcontainer.
The docs state plainly what the wrapper cannot do and how to run each check by hand.

flows.title: A coding agent finishes a turn and the stop hook runs
flows.summary: Every agent that supports a turn-end event reaches the same command, `osf hook stop`, through its own hook mechanism. The wiring differs per agent; the destination does not.

messages.label: agent turn
messages.note: The agent edits files under /workspace and produces a reply.

messages.label: stop event
messages.note: The factory profile's own plugin reads the reply from the session directly and is root-owned throughout.

messages.label: check result
messages.note: A failing check is what makes the agent's turn end with a complaint rather than a clean stop.

flows.title: A commit inside the container reaches the root-owned hooks
flows.summary: The dev user runs git, the wrapper on PATH intercepts it, forces the hooks path for repositories under the workspace mount, and the real git then runs the root-owned pre-commit and commit-msg hooks, each of which calls osf.

messages.label: refuse --no-verify / -n
messages.note: A refusal here ends the command before real git is ever reached.

messages.label: -c core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
messages.note: Only for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT; a scratch repo under /tmp is left with whatever hooks path it has.

messages.label: exit status
messages.note: A non-zero status aborts the commit.
